brief.headline: Move from 100% advance payment to normal 30-day terms and match the ₹66.48/KG price we already pay Sayaji Industries

priceAsk.summary: Ask them to match ₹66.48/KG — the price we already pay Sayaji Industries for the same Dextrose
priceAsk.basis: We're paying them ₹70.80/KG, which is 6.5% more than the ₹66.48/KG Sayaji charges us for identical material. The open market shows Dextrose asking prices of ₹60–81/kg (typically ₹66–73/kg), so our target sits right in the fair band. They need to match what we already get elsewhere.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Stop paying 100% in advance; move to standard 30-day credit terms after delivery
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Frees up ₹8.73 L of our cash that's currently locked up paying them before we even receive goods

brief.financialLeverage: Sukhjit publishes no financial statements, so we can't see their revenue, profit or cash position. That means we build our case purely on what we know: we spend ₹1.06 Cr a year with them and pay the worst terms in our book — 100% advance. We have five other confirmed makers of pharma-grade Dextrose (Sayaji already supplies us at a better price, plus Tirupati, Gulshan, Sanstar, and the global players Roquette and Ingredion) and several more leads to qualify. Without their financials, we can't judge how hard to push, so the smart move is to anchor firmly on the Sayaji benchmark and the advance-payment absurdity, while quietly lining up a second source in case they balk.

evidence.point: We already pay Sayaji Industries only ₹66.48/KG for the same material
The gap costs us an extra ₹12.95 L every year
Open-market asking prices for Anhydrous Dextrose IP run ₹60–81/kg, typically ₹66–73/kg — our target is market-fair
We pay them 100% in advance, locking up ₹8.73 L of our cash unnecessarily
India's Dextrose export price averages ₹42.95/kg — well below what we pay, showing the material isn't scarce

alternates.name: Sayaji Industries Limited (already our supplier)
alternates.why: Already gives us ₹66.48/KG — the benchmark we want Sukhjit to match; proven reliable source

alternates.name: Tirupati Starch & Chemicals Ltd
alternates.why: A lead to qualify: listed Indore maize wet-miller making Dextrose Anhydrous IV-fluid grade (exact form match); confirm IP monograph certificate of analysis before switching

alternates.name: Gulshan Polyols Ltd
alternates.why: A lead to qualify: listed starch & polyol maker, established in dextrose/sorbitol; described as drop-in alternate to our current suppliers

risks: Sukhjit doesn't publish financials, so we're flying blind on their stability — if they're fragile and we push too hard on price and terms at once, we risk losing supply before the backup is qualified
We have only two qualified Dextrose sources today (Sukhjit and Sayaji); the others are leads — so don't burn the bridge until Tirupati or Gulshan pass our audit and CoA review
Paying 100% advance gives us zero leverage if quality slips or delivery is late — fix the payment term first, then the price becomes easier to negotiate

If they refuse both asks, be ready to split the gap: offer 50% advance / 50% on delivery as a step, and phase in the price cut over two quarters to keep them at the table while we bring up the second source
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership, but paying you 100% in advance and ₹4.32 more per kilo than Sayaji charges us for identical Dextrose isn't sustainable — let's find a way to bring both into line with the rest of our supply base.
